> A device that helps keep people on track. It uses its enclosure, that is built into a rotary encoder, and e ink touch screen to save power to help remind people of there calendar. It will sync with calendar and to do apps and have display screens that will show todays event's, todos, and have a today page that mashes it all together using AI when it is connected to wifi. It will also have use a microphone for dictation to quickly make notes, reminders, and calendar events, as well as a vibration motor and a speaker for tactile and auditory output. I will use an esp32 as the the brains, with a custom circular circuit board to connect all of the hardware.

### 2026-10-02 — # Oct 2nd 2026: Researched AI

**0.75h**

# Oct 2nd 2026: Researched AI
For the AI API, I will use Google Gemini. This is because it is free, simple to use, and works straightforwardly. The prompt I will use is: "Output a 6-line daily briefing that uses a maximum of 28 characters per line. It should use ASCII only—no emojis or markdown, just plain text. The first line should be a headline, with the rest a summary of their day based on their to-dos, events, and notes. Try to connect notes to events and to-dos correctly if you can; if you are not 100% sure they are connected, do not connect them in the remaining 5 lines." Moreover, for the system prompt I will use, "You are an efficient personal secretary who accurately summarizes your client's day.""Furthermore, I will limit the token usage to just 150 to save money and tokens. Additionally, during this time, I researched how to use the Google AI APIs.

### 2026-10-03 — # Saturday October 3: Connections

**6h**

# Saturday October 3: Connections
The display's DIN pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 11. The display's CLK pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 12. The display's CS pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 10. The display's DC pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 9. The display's RST pin connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The display's SDA pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 5. The display's SCL pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 6. The display's VCC pin connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The display's GND pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The mic's SD pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 4. The mic's WS pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 3. The mic's SCK pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 2. The mic's VDD pin connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The mic's GND pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The mic's L/R pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The SD card's MOSI pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 11. The SD card's SCK pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 12. The SD card's MISO pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 13. The SD card's CS pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 1. The SD card's VCC pin connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The SD card's GND pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The encoder's CLK pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 8. The encoder's DT pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 7. The encoder's SW pin connects to the esp32 GPIO 48. The encoder's + pin connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The encoder's GND pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The speaker's IN pin connects to the esp32 RX pin. The speaker's V pin connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The speaker's G pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The 2N7000's gate pin connects to the esp32 TX pin. The 2N7000's source pin connects to the esp32 GND pin. The 2N7000's drain pin connects to the motor's − wire. The motor's + wire connects to the esp32 3V3 pin. The battery's + wire connects to the esp32 BAT+ pad. The battery's − wire connects to the esp32 BAT− pad.
